description:
Everybody has a price until they decide they don't. The strongest brands in the world don't become great because they chase every opportunity. They become great because they know what they'll never compromise. 

If a business can turn down money to protect its values, why are you willing to sacrifice your character for a promotion, a relationship, or somebody else's approval?
transcript: How many of y'all seen Chick-fil-A's in the hood? Now, I got to put it so you can understand me. They don't got them in the hood. Why? Because they're non-negotiable in Southern hospitality. So I ain't never been on 8 Mile and saw a Chick-fil-A on 8 Mile and Dequindre. I ain't never seen one. I'm just being real. I'm from the city. I ain't never seen one. Why? Because you might not get Southern what? Bro, they so deep with their values. They don't care nothing about money. We're not about to bring one of them to somewhere where you're going to be going off on people and snapping your fingers and doing your neck. It's not happening. Why? Because you're not about to mess up the brand. We'd rather take less money and be excellent than take more money and taint our brand. If a restaurant can do that, you should be able to do that with your own personal values.
